Updated request scope as of 5/17/24 refinement sent by Mr.Small:

We have put some thought into search restrictions and terms and here is what we would suggest:

(1) total time range of January 1, 2023 through July 31, 2023
(2) Anything that includes Juli Beth Hinds, Dr. Amy Lerner, urban studies and planning (USP), global policy & strategy (GPS), UCSD in conjunction with any of those terms
(3) Anything related to the regional water equity report or RDF
(4) Anything containing a reference to "Juli Beth Hinds, Dr Amy Lerner,  Geosyntec, USP, GPS, or the RWER or RDF", UCSD in conjunction with any of those terms sent to or from "Elise Ruiz, anyone at Murakawa Communications, anyone at Geosyntec including but not limited to Ken Susillo, Megan Otto, Stephanie Zinn; and anyone at the County including but not limited to Stephanie Gaines, Crystal Benham, Todd Snyder, Sarah Agassi, Eden Brukman, and Murtaza Baxamusa"

Original Request:

To Whom it may Concern:
I am writing on behalf of my client Juli Beth Hinds. On behalf of Ms. Hinds, please consider this a formal request pursuant to California Public Records Act, Government Code §6250 et seq. for copies of all DOCUMENTS of the County of San Diego Land Use & Environment Group that reference or relate to: Juli Beth Hinds; the Department of Urban Studies and Planning at the University of California San Diego; or Nathan Fletcher. ("DOCUMENTS" as used herein, shall be defined to mean any ''writing'' as that term is defined in Evidence Code section 250, including, but not limited to, correspondence, emails, texts, communications of any kind, recordings, tapes, computer print-outs, records, slides, photographs, notes, working papers, written analyses, memoranda, plans, telegraphs, telexes and transcriptions, electronic data, and notes or memoranda made by any telephone communications.) This request encompasses all DOCUMENTS dated or created between the dates of January 1, 2022 through the date of this letter.
I request delivery of these records to our firm's office, located at 402 W. Broadway, Suite 1270, San Diego, CA 92101, or we can arrange to pick them up at a reasonable location designated by the County.

Thank you for your attention to this matter.

Subject: SANDAG Vision Zero

Hello All,

Last week I met (zoom) with Staff from SANDAG re their Vision Zero Program. This program is still a work in progress and they estimate that it won’t be completed for at least the next few months.
Vision Zero<https://www.sandag.org/projects-and-programs/regional-initiatives/vision-zero>
sandag.org<https://www.sandag.org/projects-and-programs/regional-initiatives/vision-zero>
[cid:image001.png@01DAEDA7.62DC5860]<https://www.sandag.org/projects-and-programs/regional-initiatives/vision-zero>

Vision Zero is a comprehensive data driven program to identify roads/areas in our region that have the highest concentration of major accidents where law enforcement has been involved and reports have been generated.

With this accident information, these areas have then been analyzed to determine what changes or improvements could be made so that there could potentially be zero future accidents.

This information could then also be used by municipalities and the County to apply for approximately $1 billion dollars in federal grants.

One of the concerns that I have is that this data is 2 years behind, so the numbers are from 2022. It seems to me that after Covid, the public generally appears to be driving a lot faster and in a much more unsafe manner, hence an increase in accidents that these initial studies might not capture.

Below is a link for the SANDAG’s interactive map associated with this program. It shows the areas that have the highest concentration of accidents, amongst other data.
[cid:image002.jpg@01DAEDA7.62DC5860]
Traffic Safety Dashboard<https://opendata.sandag.org/stories/s/5f7y-nefe>
opendata.sandag.org<https://opendata.sandag.org/stories/s/5f7y-nefe>

While SANDAG’s goal for this program is to provide the data to help with grants, I see this as a great tool to use when we are asking DPW and TAC to reduce speeds and study roads in our area for traffic calming or other ways to reduce accidents.

I’ll keep you posted when I get further updates. If you have any questions, please let me know.

Best regards,

Eileen Delaney
Vice Chair, APG- San Diego County

emails.subject: March 12th Board Hearing on Socially Equitable Cannabis Program
emails.body:
On March 12, the Board will be hearing an item on the Socially Equitable Cannabis Program (please see attached PDF that describes the various components of the cannabis program).
Supervisor Anderson asked us to invite you to a District 2 unincorporated communities stakeholder meeting to provide you with the details of the upcoming Board vote on Tuesday, as well as the progress on other aspects of the County's cannabis policy.
Please let us know if you are available at 10 a.m. on Friday, March 8th to participate.
The Zoom link will be provided upon rsvp to gregory.kazmer@sdcounty.ca.gov<mailto:gregory.kazmer@sdcounty.ca.gov> .
As you may recall, on June 15, 2022 (7), the Board unanimously approved Supervisor Anderson's Board Letter with 16 measures to be included within the Cannabis Permitting Program Environmental Impact Report (EIR) and Socially Equitable Cannabis Program.
County staff provided Supervisor Anderson with a progress report on the community outreach and implementation the 16 measures, which we have attached for you.
The Supervisor's goal is always to provide transparency to you about what actions are coming before the Board of Supervisors and give you the opportunity to have your voice heard.
This meeting will provide the most up to date information on the County's Cannabis policy for the unincorporated areas, and how you can participate in the upcoming board meeting as well as the upcoming EIR process.
Thank you,

Greg Kazmer
Senior Land Use Advisor
District 2, Office of Joel Anderson
Cell: (858) 289-9234
